sections.h2: What are my choices for selling a house in Andover, Minnesota?
sections.html:
Owners in Andover have three paths: hire an agent and list, sell the house yourself, or take a cash offer from a buyer who accepts the property in its present condition. All three finish with a signed purchase agreement and a deed recorded in Anoka County.

One duty follows you down every path. Before you sign to sell a home, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 has you hand over a written disclosure of known material facts that could significantly hurt a typical buyer's enjoyment of the house, stated in good faith. Giving it to the buyer's agent counts as giving it to the buyer.

A cash offer tends to appeal to owners who want a short timeline, face repairs, or hold an inherited house or tenants. Get any offer in writing, and see that the number allows for tax owed and any open permits.

Andover is a city of about 33,874 people in Anoka County. That July 1, 2025 estimate from the Census Bureau is 3.9 percent above the 32,601 counted in 2020. Andover spans about 34.8 square miles, and in 2020 nearly 23 percent of residents lived in areas the census labeled rural. Median age was 39.8, with 25.8 percent of residents under 18.

The area was organized in 1857 as Round Lake Township and renamed Grow Township in 1860 after Representative Galusha Grow, who was prominent in passing the Homestead Act. For a century the population stayed small, with 757 people in 1950 and 1,402 in 1960. Then it leapt to 3,830 by 1970, 9,387 by 1980, 15,216 by 1990 and 26,588 by 2000, so nearly all of the city's growth came after 1960.

The 2020 census counted 10,782 households in Andover, and 39.4 percent of them had children under 18. The city's annual summer celebration, held in early July around City Hall, Andover Elementary and Sunshine Park, includes a 5K run, a parade and fireworks.

County Roads 9, 18, 78 and 116 are the main routes, with U.S. Highway 10 close by. Crooked Lake, on the southern border and mostly inside Coon Rapids, is the only fully recreational lake. Most of Andover belongs to Anoka-Hennepin School District 11, whose schools inside the city include Andover Elementary, Crooked Lake Elementary, Rum River Elementary, Oak View Middle School and Andover High School. A narrow northern strip falls under St. Francis Area Schools, District 15, so confirm the address before naming a district to a buyer.

sections.h2: How does Andover compare with the country on housing?
sections.html:
Andover is overwhelmingly owner-occupied, and its households are larger than the national norm. This table sets Census Bureau 2020 to 2024 estimates for the city against the country.

Household income has a median of $137,593 in 2024 dollars, and workers travel 25.4 minutes on average. The 2020 census found 11,005 housing units, 2.0 percent of them vacant, and married couples made up 71.6 percent of households. Individual streets will vary around these citywide numbers.

sections.h2: Which Andover permits matter before I sell?
sections.html:
The city's Building Department warns that work done without a needed permit has to be disclosed at sale and that code violations can delay or devalue a deal. Before listing, check your past projects against the permit list.

  • Permits are required for new construction, remodeling, additions and alterations, basement finishing, decks and porches, roofing, siding, irrigation systems and solid fuel fireplaces.
  • Plumbing permits cover water heaters and water softeners. Mechanical permits cover furnaces, air conditioners, boilers and gas fireplaces. Electrical work needs its own permit.
  • Septic systems need an installation permit and work by a Minnesota Pollution Control Agency licensed designer and installer. Pumping a septic tank takes a $20 permit that the pumper obtains.
  • No permit is needed for detached accessory structures under 200 square feet, sidewalks and patios, painting, flooring, cabinets, or normal maintenance such as replacing deck boards.

Homeowners may pull permits themselves, but the city says a licensed residential contractor is usually the better choice. Residential permits are typically approved right away or within one or two days, and about a third of permits are applied for and paid online. The Building Department is at 1685 Crosstown Blvd NW, reachable at 763-755-8700 or building@andovermn.gov.

Yes. Single family and multifamily rentals both need a city license and inspections. A license lasts two years, each rental gets at least one inspection in that span, and a new owner cannot take over the old license.

This matters when you sell a house with tenants in it. A buyer who plans to keep renting must obtain a fresh license, so mention the tenancy early. The city's rental page links to Chapter 8 of the Andover ordinances and to the Minnesota Attorney General's landlord and tenant information.

sections.h2: How do Anoka County property taxes work when an Andover house sells?
sections.html:
Anoka County prints a single statement for each parcel, mailed in mid-March. A deed recorded after January 1 does not prompt a second mailing, so the bill goes to the earlier owner, and a duplicate must be requested. A missing statement is no excuse for a late fee.

The county sets May 15 and October 15 as the dates and allows no grace period; a deadline on a weekend rolls to Monday. Online payment goes through PayAnokaCounty, with card payments at 2.6 percent and ACH e-checks at $3.50. Checks go to Property Records and Taxation, 2100 3rd Avenue, Anoka, MN 55303, or to the counter at the Government Center. A free direct payment program is explained at 763-323-5400. For mailed checks, the postmark decides timeliness, so the county advises a hand-applied one from a post office clerk.

To see what a parcel owes, search the county's property information by parcel number or by house number plus the first three characters of the street name, for example 4th rather than 4th Street. If the street shows as unassigned in the tax system, use the parcel number printed on the statement. The Government Center counter in Anoka is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, and a tax drop box sits beside it.

Two sale steps are easy to miss. A homestead owner who sells should report it to the assessor inside 30 days, or the county can strip the homestead and add penalties. At recording, a certificate of real estate value also goes to the county auditor (Minnesota Statutes 272.115). Next year's proposed statements land in mid-November and become final only after levies are approved in December.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell a house in Andover, MN?
faqs.a: It depends on the route. A listed sale waits on showings, financing and inspections, while a cash purchase removes the lender from the timeline. Either way, the written seller disclosure comes before your signature.

faqs.q: Is a permit required to swap a water heater in Andover?
faqs.a: Yes, a plumbing permit covers water heater and water softener replacement. A furnace or air conditioner falls under a separate mechanical permit.
Most of Andover is in Anoka-Hennepin School District 11. A small strip along the northern edge belongs to St. Francis Area Schools, District 15.

faqs.q: Who sends the Andover property tax statement?
faqs.a: The county does, each March, and its Property Records and Taxation office takes payment. If nothing arrives by April 1, call 763-323-5400 for a duplicate.

faqs.q: Must I tell the county when I sell my Andover home?
faqs.a: If it was your homestead, yes: report the sale to the assessor within 30 days to avoid lost homestead status and penalties. The county auditor also receives a certificate of real estate value.
